title: Voluntary Surrender Fee under Repossession and Collateral Recovery
content:
Recovery Department entry for the fee charged when a borrower gives the vehicle up voluntarily under Repossession and Collateral Recovery.

## Rule

For a case whose recovery method is voluntary surrender, the voluntary surrender fee replaces the plain class voluntary surrender fee and is figured as this rule sets out; the agency recovery fee for an involuntary recovery is figured by its own agency fee rule, and the impound release fees and every other expense on the class schedule are charged exactly as the expense schedule states.

## Booking the fee

The fee is booked with the agent-side tool `post_surrender_fee_edb82254`, which the agent unlocks and then calls.

**Capability.** The tool charges the voluntary surrender fee to a repossession case whose vehicle the borrower gave up voluntarily. One call records one new expense of kind voluntary surrender fee on the case, dated today, and raises the case's posted recovery expenses outstanding by the same amount; the new expense then shows in the case activity and the higher outstanding figure shows on the case.

**Parameters**

- `recovery_case_id` — the reference number of the repossession case the fee is charged to, as returned by the repossession case lookup for this borrower's contract (a case identifier).
- `amount_usd` — the voluntary surrender fee being charged, in US dollars as a positive decimal number with exactly 2 decimal places, already rounded to the cent; the tool stores it rounded to 2 decimal places.

**Return.** A confirmation string naming the new case activity reference number (a text identifier that begins with "rsur_"), the case reference number, the fee charged in USD with 2 decimal places, the posting date in YYYY-MM-DD form and the case's new recovery expenses outstanding in USD with 2 decimal places. A string that begins with "Surrender fee posted" means the expense was recorded.

| Recovery method on the case | Governed by this entry |
|---|---|
| Voluntary surrender | yes |
| Involuntary recovery | no |
| Impound release | no |
